ruling.reasoning:
Who cancelled is settled: the driver cancelled at 14:13:40 with reason rider_no_show, so the case runs on NS-1/NS-2, not NS-3 [F5][NS-0]. NS-1(i) is met — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40 only 40 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m radius [F7][F8][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) is met — before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 14:08:10) and made 1 in-app call (14:09), all timestamped, and the rider concedes the point [F6][F11][F13][F14][NS-1].

On NS-1(ii) the wait ran 5 minutes from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, i.e. from the 14:07:40 arrival, expiring 14:12:40; the driver cancelled at 14:13:40, 6 min 0 s after arrival, so on the recorded clock the free wait had expired [F5][F7][NS-1]. The DISP-002 8-minute threshold is not in this record, so the default 5-minute wait governs [F5][NS-1].

The decisive element is NS-1(iv). The GPS trace has no samples at all between 14:09:10 and 14:12:30, a 3 min 20 s hole that falls inside the very wait the code must measure [F1]. The stationary block 14:07:40–14:13:40 at 40 m from the pickup is recorded [F4], and cumulative time within 200 m is 6 min 25 s [F3], but neither of those bridges the untracked middle stretch: the time between two samples is not a measured wait. The trace therefore fails NS-1(iv), and a gap in the records favours neither party [F1][NS-1][TH-4]. Because continuous presence is left undecidable, the only consistent outcome is escalation with a statement of what is missing, and no amount is fixed here [F1][TH-4].

Safety screen: I read chat #1 ("I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6"), chat #2 ("More than 5 min already, I have to cancel"), the call log and the driver's statement, plus the rider's complaint — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears in any of them [F11][F12][F14][F15][F5][SAFE-1]. Nothing in the traffic or weather record raises a safety issue either [F16][F17][F18].

Profile facts were not used to decide anything: the rider's clean 90-day record and the driver's 1 upheld no-show dispute are noted only as credibility background and cannot resolve the wait condition [F19][F20][NS-1].

Correct that the item is the $5.00 fee on record and the category is system-final [F5][F9][TH-2], but no refund can be ordered while an NS-1 condition is undecidable; the outcome sought (refund_full) is not available on this record [F1][NS-2][TH-4].

The driver's reliance on DISP-002's 8-minute threshold is withdrawn by consent and is in any case not this record's threshold [F5][NS-1]. The 5-minute wait from the 14:07:40 arrival did expire at 14:12:40, so NS-1(ii) is met on the recorded clock [F7][F8].
The driver asserts all four NS-1 conditions hold, but the trace records a 3 min 20 s GPS hole during the wait, so NS-1(iv) is not proven and the fee cannot simply stand [F1][NS-1][TH-4].
The fee on record is exactly $5.00 at 1.0x, so there is no arithmetic error [F9][F10]; that does not answer whether the fee was chargeable, which is undecidable here [F1][NS-1].

System-finality of the category is about the path, not the record: an NS-1 condition left undecidable sends the case to a human under TH-4 regardless of the category's usual finality [F1][TH-2][TH-4].
